why: B (universe 0): IsGenIsoB d ↔ d.Φ.IsEquivalence, where IsGenIsoB d means some e has EquivB (d.comp e) (id X) and EquivB (e.comp d) (id Y). When Φ is an equivalence, the reversed diagram revB d hΦ (definitionally d.symm hΦ) is a two-sided inverse. The glue isGenIso_iff (IsGeneralizedIso (homMk d) ↔ IsGenIsoB d) holds by Quotient.eq and definitional composition. A_to_B uses theorem_10_3_10 alone: (1) through the glue, and for the inverse, (1) gives some two-sided inverse g and (2) says g = [d.symm hΦ]. B_to_A gets from B: theorem_10_3_10 ((2) by uniqueness of two-sided inverses with B's inverse), equiv_comp_symm, equiv_symm_comp, isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv, isIso_homMk_iff, isIso_homMk and inv_homMk. It also gets isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv_id: if d ~ 1_X then [1_X] inverts [d], by the non-item unit laws and transitivity. The other six conjuncts are proof lemmas that B does not give: the diagonal functor, two refinement facts, claims (C1)/(C2) for general functors on weak fibred products (no diagram, F not assumed an equivalence) and two M-polyfold lemmas. They are re-proved outright as copies of the project's proofs from non-item lemmas. On the text's statement the two sides agree.
